464558.name: Eastern Gamagrass (Fakahatchee) Seed
464558.short_description: Fakahatchee Grass (Tripsacum dactyloides) is a striking native perennial grass that forms dense, arching clumps up to 5–6 ft tall. Hardy in Zones 5–11, it thrives in sun to part shade and wet to dry soils — ideal for Florida-friendly landscapes, rain gardens, and native habitat restoration.
464558.description:
Fakahatchee Grass is one of the most iconic native grasses of Florida and the southeastern United States. Also known as Eastern Gamagrass, this warm-season perennial forms dense, arching clumps of bright green foliage that bring year-round structure and movement to your landscape. In subtropical climates, it stays evergreen — making it one of the few native grasses that looks great in every season.

Unlike non-native ornamental grasses, Fakahatchee Grass supports local ecosystems. Its seeds feed songbirds, quail, and wild turkeys. The dense clumps provide shelter for small mammals, reptiles, and ground-nesting birds. It serves as a larval host for the Byssus Skipper butterfly, and its inconspicuous flower spikes attract native pollinators throughout late spring and summer.

Native to Florida, the Gulf Coast, and much of the eastern U.S. from Texas to Connecticut. Thrives in full sun to partial shade and tolerates a wide range of soil moisture — from well-drained uplands to seasonally flooded sites. Once established, it is moderately drought tolerant and requires almost no maintenance. Hardy in USDA Zones 5–11, with best performance in Zones 8–11. Direct sow in spring after last frost, or cold-stratify seed at 35–40°F for 6–10 weeks before planting for best germination.

462219.name: Texas Bluebonnet Seeds
462219.short_description: Texas Bluebonnet (Lupinus texensis) — the official Texas state flower. Pre-scarified seed for reliable germination. Fall-planted winter annual that reseeds year after year.
462219.description:
Texas Bluebonnet (Lupinus texensis) is the official state flower of Texas and one of the most iconic wildflowers in North America. Each spring, Bluebonnets transform roadsides, meadows, and home gardens into seas of brilliant blue-purple color — a defining image of the Texas Hill Country and one that every Texan recognizes from childhood.

Beyond their beauty, Bluebonnets are a native legume that enriches the soil with nitrogen and provides early-season nectar for native bees and other pollinators. They reseed naturally when allowed to set seed, building a self-sustaining colony over time. Once established in the right conditions, a Bluebonnet planting comes back reliably each year with minimal care.

For best results in Texas and surrounding states, sow in fall (September–November) into a prepared, well-draining seedbed. Scarify seed before planting or purchase pre-scarified. Our 1 lb bag covers up to 200–300 sq ft in garden applications. Seed you can trust — from a team that knows Texas wildflowers.

462220.name: Texas Native Wildflower Mix
462220.short_description: 8-species native wildflower blend anchored by Texas Bluebonnet at 22%. Covers March through October with native annuals and perennials adapted to Texas soils.

462222.name: Texas Native Grass Seed Mix
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
462222.short_description: 3-species native grass blend dominated by Buffalograss at 70%. Uses 30-40% less water than Bermuda. Built for Central and West Texas alkaline soils.

462221.name: Texas Pollinator Wildflower Mix
462221.short_description: 8-species native pollinator blend with Milkweed for Monarchs, Liatris for native bees, and Scarlet Sage for hummingbirds. Blooms March through October.

462260.name: Pink Evening Primrose Seeds
462260.short_description: Pink Evening Primrose (Oenothera speciosa) — the iconic Texas pink roadside wildflower. Native perennial that creates carpets of pink blooms April through October. Drought-proof once established.

462223.name: Texas Native Pasture Prairie Mix
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
462223.short_description:
8-species native grass and wildflower blend anchored by Sideoats Grama at 35% and Little Bluestem at 25%. Built for rangeland restoration, conservation programs, and livestock pasture.

Livestock Suitability: Excellent for cattle and horses — 85% native warm-season grasses provide high-quality summer forage with heavy grazing tolerance. Good for goats. Use caution with sheep — Texas Bluebonnet (5% of mix) is a lupine species; avoid grazing sheep on young stands where wildflowers dominate. Bloat risk: Very low — only 5% legume content; bloat requires 50%+ legume pastures.

462264.name: Drummond Phlox Seeds
462264.short_description: Drummond Phlox (Phlox drummondii) — the only annual phlox native to Texas. Multicolor blooms in red, pink, purple, and white from March through May. Perfect bluebonnet companion.

462294.name: Lance Leaf Coreopsis Seed
462294.short_description: Lanceleaf Coreopsis (Coreopsis lanceolata) — Florida’s state wildflower genus. Drought-tolerant perennial with bright yellow blooms. Thrives in sandy soil. Zones 3-8.

462289.name: Florida Coastal Native Wildflower Seed Mix
462289.short_description: Focused 3-species coastal wildflower blend — Blanket Flower, Lanceleaf Coreopsis, and Spotted Beebalm. Built for Florida’s toughest sandy, coastal conditions. Zero filler.

462284.name: Grass Seed Mix for Florida Lawns
462284.short_description: Bahiagrass 50% and Bermudagrass 30% — seed your Florida lawn for a fraction of sod cost. Less water, less fertilizer, fewer bugs than St. Augustine.

462280.name: Florida Pollinator and Butterfly Seed Mix
462280.short_description: 6-species native pollinator blend with Swamp Milkweed for Monarchs, Blazing Star for native bees, and Scarlet Sage for hummingbirds. Year-round butterfly habitat for Florida.

462276.name: Florida Native Wildflower Seed Mix
462276.short_description: 7-species native wildflower blend anchored by Lanceleaf Coreopsis at 22% — Florida’s state wildflower. Covers May through October. Designed for Florida’s sandy soils.

461690.name: Pollinator Corridor Kit
461690.short_description: Create a permanent pollinator habitat with our 3-species corridor kit: Central Valley Pollinator Wildflower Mix for nectar, California Native Grass for structure, and White Clover for season-long bloom. 6.5 lbs covers ~500-2,000 sq ft.
461690.description: A 3-component habitat kit designed to create permanent pollinator corridors along field edges, fence lines, garden borders, and unused strips. Combines nectar-rich wildflowers for foraging, native bunchgrasses for nesting habitat, and White Clover for reliable season-long bloom. Ships as three separate bags.

461689.name: First-Year Color + Perennial Foundation Wildflower Kit
461689.short_description: Get wildflower color in year one and lasting perennial blooms for years to come. Annual Wildflower Mix for instant color plus Deer Resistant Mix for long-term foundation. 1 lb covers ~1,000 sq ft.
461689.description: A 2-mix wildflower kit designed to solve the biggest problem with perennial wildflower plantings: the wait. The Annual Mix provides dense color in the first growing season while the Deer Resistant Mix establishes a long-term perennial foundation underneath. Year 1 you get flowers from the annuals. Year 2 onward, the perennials take over and bloom for decades.

461687.name: Weed Smother Cover Crop Kit
461687.short_description: Smother weeds naturally with our 2-species cover crop kit: heavy Cereal Rye for allelopathic weed suppression and Mustard Biofumigant for soilborne weed seed destruction. 15 lbs covers ~5,000 sq ft.
461687.description: A 2-species weed suppression kit built around the two most aggressive weed-fighting cover crops available: Winter Cereal Rye and Mustard Biofumigant. The rye suppresses weeds from above (allelopathic chemicals + dense canopy shading) while mustard destroys weed seeds in the soil from below (glucosinolate biofumigation).

461686.name: Soil Builder Cover Crop Kit
461686.short_description: Build soil health with our 3-species cover crop kit: Winter Cereal Rye for organic matter, White Clover for nitrogen, and Mustard Biofumigant for disease suppression. 20 lbs covers ~5,000 sq ft.
461686.description: A 3-species cover crop kit that attacks soil health from three angles: Winter Cereal Rye builds organic matter and suppresses weeds, White Clover fixes nitrogen, and Mustard Biofumigant kills soilborne pathogens and nematodes. Ships as three separate bags for fall or spring planting.

461685.name: Overseed & Repair Lawn Kit
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
461685.short_description: Repair bare spots and thicken thin lawns with our 2-seed kit: Triblade Elite Tall Fescue for long-term density and Perennial Ryegrass for fast green-up. 10 lbs covers ~2,000 sq ft.
461685.description: A 2-species lawn repair kit that pairs fast-germinating Perennial Ryegrass with deep-rooted Triblade Elite Tall Fescue. The ryegrass gives you visible green in 5-10 days while the fescue fills in behind it for a dense, drought-tolerant, permanent lawn. Ships as two separate 5 lb bags.

461684.name: Thin Pasture Fix Kit
461684.short_description: Rebuild thin pastures with our 3-species kit: Perennial Ryegrass, White Clover, and Orchardgrass. 15 lbs covers approximately 10,000 sq ft. Ships as 3 separate bags for flexible application.
461684.description: A 3-species pasture renovation kit designed to fill in bare spots, thicken thin stands, and improve forage quality in degraded pastures. Ships as three separate bags — Perennial Ryegrass (5 lb), White Clover (5 lb), and Orchardgrass (5 lb) — so you can broadcast all three together or adjust ratios for your specific conditions.

458473.name: Upland Game Mix
458473.short_description: Upland Game Mix is a versatile seed blend designed for wildlife food plots and cover strips that support upland game birds like pheasants and quail from mid-summer through fall and into early winter. The blend pairs white proso millet and browntop millet (33.5% each) with buckwheat (33%), delivering a staggered, multi-seed buffet and fast-growing foliage. This combination provides continuous seed production, palatable seeds, and layered canopy structure; tall millet stems over a buckwheat understory, offering overhead concealment and lateral cover for roosting, feeding, and predator escape. Ideal for establishing dense wildlife habitat, loafing areas, and nesting cover, Upland Game Mix creates durable food and cover in a single, easy-to-manage seed solution.

458472.name: Dryland Pasture Mix
458472.short_description: Dryland Pasture Mix is engineered for semi-arid landscapes where water is scarce but pasture productivity still matters. This drought-tolerant seed blend establishes a resilient grazing stand for horses, cattle, sheep, and goats, helping you maximize forage yield on low-moisture pastures. Designed to revive overgrazed or depleted dryland fields, it creates dense forage cover that protects soil, reduces erosion, and enhances seasonal feed availability. The mix blends forage grasses and forage legumes chosen for rapid establishment, persistent growth, and compatibility with grazing systems. Whether you’re renovating neglected pastures or establishing new semi-arid pastures, Dryland Pasture Mix supports healthy, multi-species grazing with improved soil moisture retention and forage density—so you can sustain livestock with less irrigation and more resilience over time.
458472.description:
Dryland Pasture Mix is engineered for semi-arid landscapes where water is scarce but pasture productivity still matters. This drought-tolerant seed blend establishes a resilient grazing stand for horses, cattle, sheep, and other livestock across the intermountain West, High Plains, and other regions with less than 15 inches of annual precipitation.

The blend prioritizes proven dryland species: native and introduced grasses with deep root systems that tap subsoil moisture, legumes for nitrogen and palatability, and forbs that add mineral diversity to the forage base. Every species is selected for establishment success without irrigation, long-term persistence under grazing pressure, and nutritional value for a range of livestock.

Seed in early spring or late fall (dormant seeding) into a firm, weed-suppressed seedbed. Our 50 lb bag covers up to 50 acres at a light overseeding rate, or is suitable for 5–10 acres of new establishment. Developed in partnership with our in-house pasture specialists for the specific conditions of dryland ranching across the Western U.S.

458471.name: Premium Irrigated Pasture Mix
458471.short_description: Premium Irrigated Pasture Mix is a purpose-built forage blend designed for intensely managed, irrigated grazing programs. It delivers rapid establishment, dense ground cover, and high-yield production under pivot or wheel-line irrigation, supporting beef and dairy operations that practice strict rotational grazing. The mix also provides high-quality, low-dust forage for horses, making it suitable for strip grazing and sacrifice paddock recovery. Farmers and ranchers can expect improved pasture utilization, longer grazing windows, and better stand resilience across seasons. This premium seed blend tolerates irrigation variability while maintaining forage quality, rumen-friendly fiber, and steady regrowth after grazing. Ideal for multi-species pastures and high-intensity grazing plans across dairy, beef, and equestrian settings.

458469.name: Mustard Biofumigant Blend Cover Crop Seed Mix
458469.short_description: Choose the Mustard Biofumigant Blend Cover Crop Seed Mix for a fast, short-season solution to pest and disease pressure in vegetable beds. This mustard-dominant mix acts as a natural biofumigant, releasing bioactive compounds that help suppress soil-borne fungi, nematodes, and some bacterial pathogens as the mulch is incorporated. Ideal for breaking pest and disease cycles between harvests, it quickly forms dense biomass that boosts soil organic matter and soil structure. When mowed and integrated as a green manure, the blend enriches the root zone, enhances microbial activity, and improves nutrient cycling, paving the way for healthier transplants and higher yields in subsequent crops. Suitable for cool- and warm-season rotations, easy to sow, and compatible with organic systems.

458468.name: Jimmy's Perennial Wildflower Mix
458468.short_description: Jimmy’s Perennial Wildflower Mix offers a reliable, long-lasting solution for cottage-style borders that calmly return and expand each year. This versatile seed blend naturally naturalizes meadows, fence lines, and acreage edges with a low-maintenance perennial bloom display that requires minimal upkeep. Plant once for a carefree, year-round tapestry of color, texture, and pollinator-friendly nectar. The mix features a balanced selection of hardy perennials that establish quickly, spread modestly over time, and resist common garden stresses. Ideal for borders that echo traditional country gardens, pollinator habitats, and low-water landscapes. With repeated flushes of seasonal bloom, your landscape gains sustained charm without frequent replanting, erosion control, or heavy maintenance. Create welcoming, evergreen-like color that grows richer year after year.
458468.description:
Seed Mix Composition

Species % of Mix
Shasta Daisy 16%
Coreopsis, Lance-Leaved 16%
Pygmy Lupine 16%
California Poppy 10%
Western Blue-Eyed Grass 10%
Mexican Primrose 8%
Spurred Snapdragon 8%
Yarrow, Western 6%
Black-Eyed Susan 6%
Lewis Flax 4%

Why This Mix Works

Every species in Jimmy's Perennial Wildflower Mix is a true perennial — plant once and enjoy blooms that return and spread year after year. The blend is designed for maximum color diversity across spring, summer, and fall, with overlapping bloom windows so your landscape is never without flowers.

What You'll See

  • Spring: California Poppy and Pygmy Lupine lead the show with bold oranges and purples
  • Summer: Shasta Daisy, Black-Eyed Susan, and Coreopsis take over with whites and golds
  • Fall: Western Yarrow and Mexican Primrose carry color into late season

Growing Conditions

  • Sun: Full sun to partial shade
  • Water: Low to moderate — drought-tolerant once established
  • Soil: Adaptable to most well-drained soils
  • Zones: Performs across USDA zones 4–10

Planting Tips

Scatter seed on prepared soil in early spring or fall. Press gently into the soil surface — do not bury deeper than ¼ inch. Keep moist for the first 2–3 weeks until germination. Once established, these perennials require minimal watering and no fertilizer.

All seed is independently tested, filler-free, and non-GMO. Questions? Our seed experts are here to help — call 801-531-1456 or email customercare@naturesseed.com.

458467.name: Pasture Clover Mix for Waterfowl Food Plots
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
458467.short_description: Establish a high-protein pasture clover mix designed for moist or seasonally flooded fields to attract ducks, teal, and other waterfowl during migration and wintering. This seed blend provides dependable forage and seed heads for bobwhite quail and other upland game birds along pond margins, slough edges, and low pastures. The mix thrives in wet soils and gradually yields dense cover, creating a reliable food plot that sustains birds through thin forage periods. Use it to improve habitat along wetlands, farm margins, and grazing lands while delivering protein-rich forage, early-season greens, and attractive seed heads. A versatile choice for wildlife managers seeking consistent attraction and improved upland bird habitat across wet and transitional landscapes.

458434.name: Clover Lawn Alternative Mix
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
458434.short_description: A low-mow clover and microclover lawn alternative that replaces traditional grass with a soft, walkable green carpet. Stays lush with less water, no fertilizer, and far less mowing — ideal for eco-conscious homeowners.
458434.description:
The Lawn Alternative Clover Mix gives you a beautiful, low-maintenance ground cover that replaces or complements traditional turf. Blending White Dutch Clover, microclover, and complementary species, this mix forms a dense, soft-textured lawn that stays green through summer without the chemical inputs or frequent mowing that grass demands.

Clover is a natural nitrogen-fixer — it feeds itself from the air, meaning you can skip synthetic fertilizers entirely. It handles foot traffic well, tolerates drought better than cool-season grasses, and produces gentle blooms that pollinators love. This makes it a perfect choice for families, dog owners, and anyone who wants a functional, low-cost lawn that's also good for the environment.

Our blend is expertly proportioned for quick establishment and season-long coverage. Seed in spring or fall into a prepared seedbed. Works as a standalone lawn or blended into existing turf for a natural, sustainable upgrade.

458047.name: Hardy Grass Seed Mix for High Traffic Lawns
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
458047.description: Find a premium grass seed mix that is ideal for high traffic lawns and will stand up to abuse from dogs, kids, and more. Our hardy mix features top-rated varieties that are drought tolerant and create dense, durable turf.

456233.name: Sundancer Buffalograss Lawn Seed
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
456233.short_description: Sundancer Buffalograss is a native, warm-season lawn grass that stays green and beautiful with up to 75% less water than conventional turf. Perfect for drought-prone regions, it requires minimal mowing and no synthetic inputs once established.
456233.description:
Sundancer Buffalograss (Bouteloua dactyloides) is one of the most water-efficient lawn grasses available — a native North American species naturally adapted to heat, drought, and hard clay soils. Sundancer is a selected cultivar bred specifically for improved density, color, and wear tolerance compared to wild-type buffalograss, making it a genuine premium lawn option for water-conscious homeowners across the Great Plains and Southwest.

Once established, Sundancer needs irrigation only during extended drought — dramatically reducing your water bill and maintenance time. It grows to a tidy 4–6 inch height without mowing, turns a rich blue-green through summer, and goes naturally dormant (tan) in winter before greening back up in spring. No fertilizers, no pesticides, and no constant watering required.

This is a warm-season grass best suited to USDA Zones 3–9 in the central and western U.S. Seed in late spring when soil temps exceed 60°F. Our 3 lb kit covers up to 600 sq ft of new lawn or larger areas as a mix with other native species.

455414.name: Green Screen Food Plot Mix
455414.short_description: A high-attraction food plot seed blend designed to hold deer and wildlife on your property through fall and winter. Fast-establishing annuals and perennials provide reliable forage from early season through hard frosts.
455414.description:
Green Screen Food Plot Mix is engineered to attract and hold deer, turkey, and other wildlife from early fall through late season. The blend combines fast-germinating annuals with persistent perennials to give you green, palatable forage exactly when hunting pressure peaks and natural food sources decline.

The mix includes species proven to draw heavy browse pressure: brassicas for cool-season attraction, clovers for warm-season protein, and grains that remain standing through early frosts. Together they create a food plot that produces from the first cool nights of fall through the end of deer season — giving wildlife a reason to stay on your land.

Seed into a well-prepared seedbed in late summer for fall establishment. The 10 lb kit covers approximately one acre in average soil conditions. Developed by Nature's Seed wildlife specialists with regional foraging behavior in mind.

455409.name: Krunch N Munch Food Plot Mix

452706.name: Premium Pet & Kid Friendly Bluegrass Bundle

452626.name: Pet & Kid Friendly Low-Maintenance Fescue Lawn Bundle
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest

452364.name: White Clover Seed
452364.description: White clover (Trifolium repens) is one of the most valuable and versatile plants you can add to your pasture, lawn, or food plot. This low-growing perennial legume is prized worldwide for its ability to naturally enrich soil through nitrogen fixation, reducing the need for synthetic fertilizer and boosting the growth of surrounding grasses. White clover forms a dense, spreading mat of foliage that can reach up to 12 inches in height, making it an ideal ground cover for erosion control, weed suppression, and improving soil health over time.

451810.name: White Dutch Clover Soil & Grass Health Boost - 5lb for 10,000 Sq ft.

450588.name: Rice Hulls: Improve Seed Contact, Germination & Hold Moisture

450345.name: Rice Hulls
450345.description:
M-Binder tackifier is a botanical glue used in hydroseeding, to stabilize soils and for dust control. Derived from the seed of the plantego plant (Plantago insularis), M-Binder is 100% organic, non-toxic and biodegradable. Use anywhere you need to “tack” down seed, straw or mulch, or to control dust and erosion. Works great for revegetation and restoration projects, fire rehabilitation, landscaping and beautification.

Application

M-Binder may be applied as a dry powder or as wet slurry to dry or wet surfaces. It may even be applied during rain. It does not require set-up or drying time because when it is wet it is a heavy muciloid material and when dry it is a firm but rewettable membrane.

Application Rates

General Use: 60-140 lbs. per acre (approx. 1.5 - 3.25 lbs./1000 sq. ft.)

Mixed with Wood Fiber or Paper Mulch: 80-100 lbs. per acre

Dust Control Applications: 150-200 lbs. per acre

447115.name: Sun and Shade Grass Seed Mix
categories: Drought-Tolerant Lawn Seeds — Built for CA, AZ, OR & the Southwest
447115.short_description: Conquer the shady, humid climate of the American Northeast with this special mix of Kentucky bluegrass and fescue seed. Together these grasses provide quick establishment and a beautiful, dark green lawn anywhere in this area of the country.
447115.description:
Sun and Shade Grass Seed Mix is a balanced blend of Kentucky Bluegrass, creeping red fescue, and perennial ryegrass designed to perform across the full range of light conditions — from full-sun open lawns to partially shaded areas under trees and along building foundations. Most lawns have both, and this blend adapts to them all.

Kentucky Bluegrass provides the fine-textured, dense turf that self-repairs through underground rhizomes. Fine fescues thrive in shade and low-fertility soils where bluegrass struggles. Perennial ryegrass germinates in as few as 5–7 days, providing quick cover while the slower species establish. Together, they create a resilient, self-balancing lawn that fills in naturally based on where each species performs best in your yard.

This blend is expertly proportioned for the Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Upper Midwest — regions with humid summers and cold winters where a diverse mix outperforms single-species plantings. Seed in early fall for optimal establishment. Our mix is filler-free, independently tested, and backed by Nature's Seed's germination guarantee.

445350.name: California Poppy
445350.short_description: California Poppy (Eschscholzia californica) is the iconic golden wildflower of the Western U.S., beloved for its brilliant orange blooms, extreme drought tolerance, and ease of establishment. Perfect for meadows, roadsides, and low-water garden beds.
445350.description:
California Poppy is one of the easiest and most rewarding wildflowers you can grow. Native to California and the Southwest, this annual and short-lived perennial thrives in poor, dry soils where other plants struggle — blooming reliably from spring through fall with minimal care. Its brilliant gold and orange flowers close at night and open with the morning sun, creating a dynamic, living display that pollinators and people both love.

Once established, California Poppy reseeds prolifically, building a self-sustaining colony that returns year after year. It requires no irrigation once established, needs no fertilizer, and handles the heat of California summers without the stress that wilts most flowers. This makes it an ideal choice for xeriscaping, meadow restoration, and wildfire recovery seeding across the Western U.S.

Sow seed directly in fall or early spring into a prepared, weed-free seedbed. Scatter seed and lightly press into soil — do not cover, as California Poppy needs light to germinate. Our pure seed is independently tested for germination and free of filler species or grasses.

445349.name: Coastal California Wildflower Seed Mix
445349.short_description: A stunning blend of California coastal native wildflowers selected for drought tolerance, salt spray resistance, and year-round bloom interest. Brings vibrant color to coastal gardens, roadsides, and restoration sites while supporting native bees and pollinators.
445349.description:
The Coastal California Wildflower Mix brings together native wildflower species specifically adapted to California's coastal climate: cool summers, mild winters, salt-laden air, and the lean, sandy or clay soils common to coastal bluffs and hillsides. Every species in this blend is tested for performance in coastal conditions — not just California overall, but the specific challenge of the coastal zone.

The mix includes a rich diversity of annual and perennial natives that bloom in succession from early spring through summer, providing a continuous color display and a reliable nectar source for native bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds. Species are selected to reseed naturally and build in density over time, reducing maintenance needs each season.

Ideal for coastal home gardens, restoration projects, and Cal Fire defensible space zones. Seed in fall (October–December) to take advantage of winter rains for natural germination. Our blend is collected from California ecotypes where possible, expertly tested for coastal adaptability, and packaged filler-free for pure, predictable results.

445347.name: Narrowleaf Milkweed Seed
445347.short_description: Narrowleaf Milkweed (Asclepias fascicularis) is the essential Western U.S. host plant for Monarch butterflies. Plant it to support Monarch migration, provide nectar for native bees, and restore native pollinator habitat in your garden or landscape.
445347.description:
Narrowleaf Milkweed is the native milkweed of choice for most of the Western United States. Unlike Tropical Milkweed (Asclepias curassavica), which can disrupt Monarch migration patterns, Narrowleaf Milkweed is a true native perennial that goes dormant in winter — naturally cuing Monarchs to continue their migration south. Planting native milkweed is one of the most impactful things you can do for Monarch butterfly conservation.

Beyond Monarchs, Narrowleaf Milkweed's small pink and white flower clusters are rich in nectar and attract a wide range of native bees, beetles, and other beneficial insects. It spreads slowly by underground rhizomes to form a naturalized colony over time, providing reliable, low-maintenance pollinator habitat that improves each year.

Native to California, Oregon, Washington, Nevada, and neighboring western states. Thrives in well-drained soils, full sun, and is highly drought tolerant once established. Direct sow in fall for natural cold stratification, or cold-stratify seed for 30 days before spring planting. Our pure seed is sourced from Western U.S. ecotypes for the best regional adaptation.

445346.name: Microclover Seed (Micro Clover, Mini Clover)
445346.short_description:
Many years of natural selection have resulted in revolutionary micro-clovers with all the benefits of traditional clover packed into very tiny leaves. Microclover® “spoon feeds” nitrogen to the grass, producing a healthy, dense and naturally green lawn. Helps out-compete weeds, and keeps grass green all season long.

  • All the benefits of traditional white clover packed into very tiny leaves.
  • Tolerates closer mowing than standard white clover.
  • Acts as a natural source of fertilizer.
  • Comes coated and inoculated.

445330.name: Am 120 Standard Mycorrhizal Inoculant
445330.description:
AM 120 Standard is a premium arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) inoculant containing 100% Rhizophagus intraradices(formerly Glomus intraradices), delivering 300 propagules per gram. It’s designed to form a symbiotic relationship with plant roots—extending hyphae networks throughout the soil to enhance water, phosphorus, and micronutrient uptake, improve drought tolerance, and boost germination and biomass production .

Common applications include:

  • Native plant and ecological restoration – excellent for reforestation, slope stabilization.

  • Nursery/greenhouse seedling production – pre-colonize seedlings in trays or pots (e.g., 5 lb per yd³ medium).

  • Agriculture & row crops – side-dress seed furrows or transplant holes at 5–8 lb/acre (or per 30–40″ row); broadcast for cereals, legumes, and vegetables .

  • Turf, lawns, and hydroseeding – spread 1–2 lb per 1,000 ft² or 60 lb/acre; effective with native meadow or turf seeding .

Best Paired With

To maximize the benefits of AM 120:

  1. Direct root contact
    Apply at planting, mixing with seed, or placing around root balls to ensure spores touch roots—dry broadcasting alone limits effectiveness .

  2. Low-to-moderate phosphorus soils
    High phosphorus levels hinder colonization—avoid over-fertilizing before or during application.

  3. Healthy organic soil or growing media
    Use with good-quality potting mixes or tilled topsoil to support fungal establishment; avoid overly sterilized environments .

  4. Complementary sustainable practices
    Pair with minimal tillage, crop rotation, cover crops, and organic amendments to strengthen native soil microbial communities .

How It Works

  • Forms an extensive network of hyphae expanding the root’s reach far beyond its physical extent.

  • Enhances uptake of immobile nutrients like phosphorus, zinc, and copper; improves water access and drought resistance .

  • Stimulates soil structure and carbon sequestration, producing glomalin “soil glue” that enhances water retention and carbon storage .

  • Promotes plant growth, survival, and yield, especially in seedlings and stressed soils; USGS trials confirmed improved germination or biomass in over 70% of tested species .

Guide to Using AM 120

Application Situation Rate & Application Method
Broadcast / Lawn & Seed Spread 1–2 lb per 1,000 ft² (≈60 lb/acre); lightly incorporate or cover with mulch, then water .
Row crops / transplants Side‑dress 5–8 lb/acre in seed furrow or transplant hole; cover with soil at 2–6″ depth .
Nursery media Mix evenly at 5 lb per cubic yard (≈300 k propagules/yd³) .
Hydroseeding / restoration Blend inoculum with seed and organic fertilizer in first slurry pass; mulch afterwards .
Established plants Use root drench or soil injection (e.g., turkey baster) around drip zone—ensure contact, don’t rely on foliar use .

Best Practices

  • Timing: Apply at planting or transplanting for optimal colonization; inoculating established plants requires soil injection near roots.

  • One-time application: Once colonized, additional inoculation isn’t necessary unless soil is disturbed or sterilized.

  • Minimize phosphorus fertilizer: High phosphorus can suppress fungal establishment.

  • Keep spores viable: Avoid sunlight and store in a cool, dry place; handle with a dust mask when dry .

Why Choose AM 120 Standard?

  • Proven single‑species effectiveness across climates from Canada to Costa Rica .

  • High propagule density ensures robust colonization and quicker root‑fungi networks .

  • Versatility for ecological restoration, agriculture, turf, and nursery use.

  • Supports sustainable soil health—enhanced nutrient efficiency, water retention, carbon storage, and soil structure.

  • Humus and organic matter – Adds ~5 % humates, enhancing cation exchange and water retention; buffers pH and suppresses pathogens .

  • Supports root establishment – Ideal in-furrow starter for agronomic crops, bedding plants, and lawn seed.

Guide on Using Organic Seed Starter 4‑6‑4

Scenario Timing & Method
Seed trays or blocks Mix into starter medium before sowing (at ~¼ tsp per 4″ pot) for steady nutrient release
Outdoor vegetable beds Broadcast 1 cup per 10 sq ft (≈1 lb N/1,000 sq ft), dig into top 4″ before planting .
Transplants Place ¼ cup in hole or ring around base before transplanting seedlings .
New lawns & sod Spread 25 lb per 1,000 sq ft, thoroughly water, and maintain soil moisture for 2 weeks .
Landscape/new plantings Apply 10–15 lb per 1,000 sq ft before seeding or planting; repeat applications 2–3× per season .

Seedling Feeding Tips

  • Start feeding when seedlings are ~2″ tall with 2 true leaves. Apply at quarter strength or mix into soil to avoid root stress .

  • Avoid overfeeding – slow-release, compost-based nutrients are gentle yet effective; monitor soil moisture and coloration.

  • Post-germination boost – Water in well after application to activate nutrient uptake and maximize root-zone efficacy.

Why Choose 4‑6‑4 Organic Seed Starter?

  • Balanced nutrient profile with elevated phosphorus supports robust root growth.

  • Safe and certified organic, compliant with whole-food growing standards.

  • Boosts soil health long-term, with humates and microbial content enhancing soil structure and fertility.

  • Versatile application across gardening, landscaping, turf care, and ecological restoration projects.

  • When to Plant: Early spring or late summer when highs are between 60–75°F.

  • Under patios, pergolas, and garden structures
